cells.tense: You are already blending what to keep and what to release, and it is holding.
cells.act: teach it the way it was taught to you, with one change
cells.ask: Take something you do well because somebody showed you how. Show one other person, keep their way of learning ahead of yours, and change a piece of it to fit who they are. Then let it be theirs.
cells.core:
When you are standing in this — releasing what has done its work and keeping what still feeds you — the mix runs without being managed. It is a hand that lets go of one thing as it takes up another, so the hand is not full and not empty for long. Whoever is near you feels steadier for it.

What you can pass on, you can pass on without trapping anybody in it. Pick one practice you were handed, and hand it on with a change in it — the change is the sign that you are alive in the middle of it, not preserving. This one cannot be done alone. A tradition only continues when somebody else is standing with you. Which part would you want them to keep?
cells.sheetLine: You can pass something on without trapping anyone in it.
cells.verb: sensing what to add, what to subtract, and how to blend, moment by moment
cells.place: on the letting-go side, where release makes room

cells.tense: You will have papered over the next disagreement before it is spoken.
cells.ask: Before the next moment where the table could stay comfortable, name what you actually want and go get it. Not sharply — just first, before you've worked out how they will take it.
cells.core:
The pull here is to keep the table smooth, get the same page under everybody early, and the real point slides out of view. Two people who disagree don't get to hear each other, and neither is told the truth. That smoothing is not peace. It is a lid, and things under a lid keep growing.

What settles this is movement, not more blending. Go straight at what you want — not the version you would have to defend — and say it, then watch what the others do with that. You can hold your own feeling while you do it. That is allowed, and it is not the same as keeping the lid on. Something real goes forward, and you find out whether the calm can take a person.
cells.sheetLine: You're smoothing the room before anyone says the real thing.

cells.tense: Every room you stand in pulls the middle of you somewhere else.
cells.act: sit with someone in it without fixing it
cells.ask: Find somebody in something hard right now. Stay with them a while and don't fix it, don't advise, don't match it. Keep your own edge. Leave when you said you would.
cells.core:
The center that would hold a mixed day doesn't come. Each thing that pulls does pull, and you go with it, and by evening you would be hard put to say what you thought about any of it. That is not a flaw in you. It is what happens when nothing has been let go — a hand that stays closed cannot hold anything else.

The one reliable way back runs through another person, and not by talking about them. Stay with somebody in something real — no fixing, no merging, your edge kept. The staying is what settles you, and it settles from the side. Nobody has to do it perfectly for it to work.
cells.sheetLine: Each thing that pulls pulls the middle of you with it.

cells.tense: You are already letting one thing go, and you call it no decision.
cells.act: learn how the people before you did it
cells.ask: Pick a thing you keep doing because it was shown to you that way. Before you're sure it means what you think, go find out how it was done before your time — ask, watch, or read. Then decide what stays.
cells.core:
Asked, you would say you mostly keep on with things. But something is thinning out around you — a way of marking a season, or a phrase a group says with nobody's hand on it — and the hand on it is yours. Not loudly. You are simply not renewing it, and the gap is doing the deciding for you.

Go behind it. Find out how the old ones kept the same thing, and set their version next to yours. You may keep yours exactly as it is — that is a real answer. But it becomes a choice with your name on it instead of a drift with nobody's, and the thing gets either a real edge or a real anchor. Both hold.
cells.sheetLine: You're already letting things go and calling it no decision.

cells.place: on the letting-go side, where release makes room

attempts.check: The draft's riskiest claim is that the person is currently steering something they author — for Unacknowledged the record only supports authorship being misattributed, never that the thing is old, costly, or that anyone taught them; I've kept every line to what a moment would show. A reader could fairly say the scattered days aren't a fragmentation but grief or logistics, so each ask is written to stand on its own whether or not my read is right — each teaches the person something even unnamed and isn't conditional on my being correct. The sentence serving me more than them was any line about 'calibration' or 'equilibrium'; I cut them all — the strongest self-serving risk is sounding wise about balance instead of naming one recognisable moment. The four asks open on four verbs — blend, begin, sit, learn — and none paste the record's phrasing for five words.
